subject: Evidence request: data lifecycle retention and erasure controls
messages:
From: Tom Willis <tom.willis@acme.co>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: acmecorp-security@acme.co, Lara Nguyen <lara.nguyen@acme.co>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence pull: retention & deletion controls for SOC 2/ISO attestation

Hi Ben,

We're starting the evidence collection for Acme's annual SOC 2 and ISO 27001 attestation and need Redwood's artifacts around data residency, retention configuration, and deletion/erasures. The auditor is focused on two areas: (1) demonstrable retention schedules and automated enforcement (S3 lifecycle, DB TTLs, backups) and (2) evidence that customer data is fully removed on request (deletion logs, runbooks, verification).

Could you provide the following items (timeboxed to the last 12 months unless noted):
- A copy of the retention policy applied to Acme's tenant and the enforcement mechanisms (config snippets or policy exports)
- Deletion runbook and step-by-step evidence for completed erasure requests (sample redaction/deletion jobs)
- Logs showing completed erasure jobs for the period 2026-01-01 through 2026-06-14 (hashed identifiers okay)
- Proof of cross-region residency settings for Acme's tenant (which regions hold customer data)
- Any related encryption/KMS key deletion or key-rotation artifacts relevant to deletion proofs

We attached the auditor's questionnaire (short spreadsheet) — please let me know if you need an NDA update or a secure link for large files. Auditor turnover is tight; can we aim to have an initial evidence bundle by end-of-day Wednesday (2026-06-16)?

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Willis
Senior Information Security Manager
Acme Corp

Attachment: acme_evidence_questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet, 53KB)

Thanks Ben — quick update and clarification requests for Acme's auditor so we provide precise artifacts: 

What we can deliver by EOD Wed (2026-06-16):
- Redwood retention policy text and the tenant-level retention config that was active for Acme (export: redwood_s3_lifecycle_policy.txt)
- Deletion runbook (deletion_runbook_v2.pdf) describing steps, checks, and verification criteria for erasure requests
- Sample deletion job evidence: kvcache_deletion_log_20260101-20260614.csv (hashed keys, timestamps, status) — we will redact any raw token content and provide hashed identifiers only
- Residency mapping: statement of region assignments and a CSV mapping tenants->regions (we will include Acme's assigned region(s) and replication topology)

Clarifications / asks from the auditor: 
1) Do they need logs at the object-level (S3 object names) or are hashed IDs sufficient for their reconciliation? We prefer hashed IDs for customer privacy.
2) If they need time-of-deletion snapshots (post-deletion verification checks), we can provide job run outputs showing job completion and verification step results (we need to know acceptance criteria).
3) Regarding backups: our documented retention for backups is covered in the policy doc; if the auditor requires backup restore-tests as deletion evidence, we'll need an additional window to schedule a restore and test (not included in the EOD bundle).

I'll prepare the artifacts and upload to a shared Drive folder with restricted access. Ben / Monica — please confirm whether Acme has an active shared-drive exception or whether we should request a secure S3 presigned transfer instead.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of InfoSec (Compliance) | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_s3_lifecycle_policy.txt (policy export, 4KB)
